manifest.name: @trujaycc/dsh-weixin-minigame
manifest.description: Preview in dsh's built-in browser, debug (logs and screenshots), and publish WeChat Mini Games inside the dsh Web GUI, through the official mini game helper service

scripts.prepublishOnly: pnpm run build && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run test

bundle.text:
# @trujaycc/dsh-weixin-minigame bundle patch.
#
# Two inserted rows: the plugin's own node half (skill + preview-status route),
# and the MCP bridge that gives the agent the WeChat Mini Game tools. One bare
# row then re-enables the surface the preview opens in.
#
# Install into a profile with:
#   dsh plugin --profile <name> add @trujaycc/dsh-weixin-minigame
# New rows are added through `insert` (a bare row targets an existing row by
# id). The plugin row mounts the node half; its browser half is advertised and
# served through the package's dsh.client manifest.

- insert:
    # The skill and the /minigame/status route the browser half polls before it
    # opens the preview in the built-in browser.
    # Nothing here is per-session: the host skill registry reaches every session
    # of every agent preset.
    - id: weixin-minigame
      name: '@trujaycc/dsh-weixin-minigame'

    # MCP bridge to the upstream mini game helper server (preview server, wx
    # API compatibility layer, and miniprogram-ci upload). Tools reach the
    # model as mcp__minigame__run_game, mcp__minigame__get_logs,
    # mcp__minigame__real_device_preview, mcp__minigame__publish, and so on.
    #
    # The upstream version is PINNED on purpose. With @latest, every boot
    # fetched and executed whatever upstream had published by then, in every
    # user's environment, with no review step here. Bump this deliberately:
    # check the upstream release, then run this package's tests before
    # changing the pin.
    # failOnStartupError is false on purpose: this server is installed on
    # demand by npx and needs network access, and a machine without either
    # must not lose its whole Web session to a failing MCP handshake. A failed
    # startup leaves the bridge without tools and logs the reason.
    - id: minigame-mcp
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: minigame
        transport: stdio
        command: npx
        args:
          - '-y'
          - '--prefer-online'
          - '@weadmin/weixin-minigame-helper-mcp@0.1.35'
        failOnStartupError: false
        # The client's default tool-call timeout is 60s, which is shorter than
        # three upstream tools legitimately take: packaging a game, uploading a
        # version, and a burst screenshot capture the caller may ask to run for
        # up to 60s by itself. Five minutes still bounds a hung call.
        toolCallTimeoutMs: 300000

# The preview opens in dsh's built-in browser tab. The web-app bundle ships
# that tab type but leaves it disabled outside Desktop ("Web profiles opt in"),
# so this bundle turns it on for every profile it composes into. Desktop
# already has it on and the same override is a no-op there.
- id: ui-sidebar-browser
  disabled: false

readme.text:
English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Preview, develop, and debug (through logs and screenshots) WeChat Mini Games inside the dsh Web GUI. The preview runs in dsh's built-in browser tab; the plugin adds no window of its own. Modelled on the official [WeChat Mini Game Helper](https://gamemp.weixin.qq.com/doc/minigame-helper/guide/vscode-plugin.html).

| Surface | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Browser preview** | The mini game opens in dsh's built-in browser tab in the right sidebar, which supplies history, reload, and the address bar. The helper's own preview page supplies the ⚙️ configuration and QR dialogs. Both the preview and the credentials are managed by the official mini game helper service; this plugin neither stores nor uploads anything. |
| **`weixin-minigame-helper` skill** | Guidance for the MCP tools and this plugin, and for the game development workflow. |
| **MCP bridge** | Connects dsh to the mini game helper service. |

| You want to | Example prompt |
| --- | --- |
| See the game running | "Bring the mini game project in the current workspace up so I can look at it" |
| Fix a crash or a blank screen | "Preview the current workspace mini game and keep fixing until the log is clean" |
| Check what the frame actually renders | "Take a screenshot after that change so I can see it" |
| Try it on a real phone | "Run a real-device test on the current workspace mini game" |
| Ship a version | "Publish the current workspace mini game as 1.0.1, note: score fix" |

| Capability | Backing MCP tools |
| --- | --- |
| Start or hot-reload the preview | `run_game` |
| Read console output and errors | `get_logs` |
| Capture the rendered frame, single or burst | `capture_screenshot`, `capture_screenshot_burst`, `stop_screenshot_burst` |
| Real-device QR preview | `real_device_preview` |
| Upload a version to the WeChat platform | `publish` |
| Platform launch workflow — game info, filing, qualification, version submission | `open_onboarding` and the `mp_*` family |

- Requires: dsh Web, Node `^22.19.0` or `>=24.0.0` (the same range dsh itself requires), npx
- Not required: WeChat DevTools (install it if you want to debug code yourself)

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @trujaycc/dsh-weixin-minigame
```

Then **restart `dsh web`**: the client-module registry caches package metadata for the life of the process, so a newly added row is only discovered at the next boot. After that, edits to `lib/client.js` reload on their own through the always-mounted client HMR chain.

readme.section: From a local checkout (developing this plugin)
readme.text:
```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run build
dsh plugin --profile web add <absolute path to this plugin>
```

Installing from a **directory** creates a link to the checkout, so a later `pnpm run build` takes effect without reinstalling. The first activation still needs the `dsh web` restart above.

To verify what npm would actually publish, use a tarball instead:

```sh
pnpm pack
dsh plugin --profile web add ./trujaycc-dsh-weixin-minigame-0.1.0.tgz
```

readme.section: From a local checkout (developing this plugin)
readme.text: A tarball is an unpacked copy, so later code changes need another `pnpm pack` and a reinstall.

- A WeChat Mini Game directory containing `game.js`.
- Real-device preview and publish additionally need a WeChat **AppID** and an **upload private key**, configured through the ⚙️ button in the preview page; see the [official documentation](https://gamemp.weixin.qq.com/doc/minigame-helper/guide/vscode-plugin.html).

One skill joins the session catalog — `weixin-minigame-helper`, described as the preview/repair loop for WeChat mini game code. Its body is loaded only when the model calls the `skill` tool; the catalog itself carries the name and description alone, capped by the harness's catalog limit.

No system-prompt section is registered, so nothing is paid on unrelated turns. The MCP tool schemas come from the upstream service and are registered only after a successful handshake; a bridge that fails to start merely leaves those tools absent and does not affect dsh startup.

A trigger button joins the top-right of the session header (the lamp on its left is green while a project is running, grey when idle, and hollow when the plugin is not mounted). Clicking it opens — or reopens — the preview in dsh's built-in browser tab in the right sidebar; the tab also opens automatically the first time a packaged game is served. dsh's browser supplies back/forward/reload and the address bar, and nothing floats over the conversation.
The bundle patch enables dsh's `ui-sidebar-browser` row, because Web profiles ship it disabled by default; Desktop already has it on, so the override changes nothing there.

- **The upstream MCP server is a third-party dependency.** It is fetched by `npx` at boot, with the version pinned in `cordis.patch.yml` (currently `0.1.35`). Tool names, parameters, and behaviour can change with an upstream release, so run this plugin's tests before bumping that pin.
- **The official mini game helper service leaves files in the game project** (screenshots, and so on). Add them to `.gitignore` yourself.
- **One preview server per machine, shared across dsh instances and other hosts.** The helper records where it listens in a single file under the user's home directory, and the first process to bind takes the default port, so a second process using the helper (another dsh instance, or the official editor extension) overwrites that record and serves on the next free port.
- **The preview needs dsh's built-in browser.** This bundle enables the `ui-sidebar-browser` row; disabling that row again leaves the trigger unable to open a tab. The tab opens automatically only while a Conversation is on screen — after returning to one, the next status poll opens it.
- **The preview status is readable by any caller on the loopback interface.** It exposes nothing but a local addre

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm run build    # emits lib/index.js and lib/client.js (ModuleLoader handoff)

The client bundle resolves `react` from the dsh Web loader's platform module table and declares no other runtime dependency.

`pnpm run watch` rebuilds `lib/client.js` on change; the client HMR chain reloads the plugin in the browser without a page refresh.

The workflow this plugin guides the agent through, and the way it drives the MCP server, are modelled on the official [WeChat Mini Game Helper](https://gamemp.weixin.qq.com/doc/minigame-helper/guide/vscode-plugin.html).

The MCP service is `@weadmin/weixin-minigame-helper-mcp`. It is fetched with `npx` at runtime and is not redistributed with this package.
